summary: Worktrees add lifecycle and dependency-state complexity and are unnecessary when agents only inspect data or edit strictly disjoint generated artifacts.

points.text: Shared package caches, ignored files and repository-local databases can still couple supposedly isolated worktrees in surprising ways.
Large dependency installations per tree can consume substantial disk and setup time unless caches are designed safely.
A worktree prevents accidental file-state collision but cannot prevent two agents from making incompatible decisions about the same API or requirement.
